inspectionBanner.title: Before You Begin
inspectionBanner.line1: Verify vehicle has passed Texas state inspection
inspectionBanner.line2: Confirm customer has valid auto insurance
inspectionBanner.line3: Both must be current before completing paperwork

step1.title: Driver License Copy
step1.why: Texas law requires dealer to verify and retain a copy of the buyer's government-issued photo ID. Often arrives via the customer portal after the Bill of Sale link is sent.
step1.task1: Take a clear photo or photocopy of the driver license
step1.task2: Verify name on DL matches the name on the Bill of Sale
step1.task4: Check if a copy is already on file from a previous transaction
step1.task5: Tip: If you've already sent the Bill of Sale link via SMS, the buyer may have uploaded their ID through the customer portal. Check there first

step2.title: Bill of Sale
step2.why: The Bill of Sale is the primary legal document transferring vehicle ownership from dealer to buyer.
step2.task1: Verify all vehicle information is correct (VIN, year, make, model, mileage)
step2.task2: Confirm buyer information matches their driver license
step2.task3: Review financial details: sale price, fees, tax, total due
step2.task4: Obtain all required signatures (buyer, co-buyer if applicable, dealer rep)
step2.task5: Verify all acknowledgments are initialed or checked

step3.title: Buyer's Guide
step3.why: FTC requires all used car dealers to display a Buyer's Guide on every vehicle and provide a copy to the buyer at sale. In most cases the customer already signed this during the Bill of Sale portal flow (Step 2). Just verify it's on file.
step3.task1: Check the Bill of Sale portal submission. The Buyer's Guide acknowledgment is bundled into it
step3.task2: Verify the vehicle info on the guide matches the Bill of Sale (year, make, model, VIN)
step3.task3: Confirm the 'AS IS. No Dealer Warranty' box is marked
step3.task4: If the customer didn't complete the portal flow, print and hand-sign a paper Buyer's Guide copy
step3.task5: File the dealer copy with the rest of the deal paperwork

step4.title: Form 130-U
step4.why: Texas Application for Title requires exact information matching the vehicle title. Errors cause title rejection.
step4.task1: Vehicle description must match the title exactly
step4.task2: Buyer name and address must match their driver license
step4.task3: Complete the seller section with dealer information
step4.task4: Odometer reading must match the Bill of Sale
step4.task5: Both buyer and seller must sign and date the form

step5.title: Title Transfer
step5.why: The vehicle title is the legal proof of ownership. Incorrect handling causes delays and legal issues with TxDMV.
step5.task1: Front of title: stamp 'SURRENDERED' across the face
step5.task2: Back of title: both seller and buyer sign in the correct fields
step5.task3: Verify addresses match on title and 130-U
step5.task4: Odometer reading matches Bill of Sale and 130-U
step5.task5: Decide: sign back of title directly OR use reassignment section
step5.task6: If using reassignment: stamp the next empty reassignment section
step5.usedReassignment: Used a reassignment section on the title
step5.signedTitleBack: Signed directly on the back of the title
step5.titleWarning: CRITICAL: A title can only be reassigned a limited number of times. Once all reassignment sections are used, the title must be sent to TxDMV for a new title before the vehicle can be sold again. Verify which section to use BEFORE signing.
step5.helpTitle: What is a Dealer's Reassignment of Title?
step5.helpBody: When a dealer buys a vehicle at auction (or from another dealer) and resells it without ever titling it in the dealer's own name, Texas law lets the dealer "reassign" the existing title directly to the new buyer using the Dealer's Reassignment of Title form (TxDMV VTR-41-A). This form has three reassignment blocks stacked on the page. Each block has space for a seller (the dealer) + purchaser (the next owner) + odometer reading + signatures. Once all three blocks are used, the title must be sent to TxDMV for a clean re-issued title before the vehicle can be sold again.
step5.helpSteps: Fill out the next unused block only. Enter the VIN, year, make, body style, and model at the top; dealership name and license number; seller + purchaser names and addresses; the current odometer reading (no tenths); and both signatures with the date. Leave the remaining blocks blank for the next dealer in the chain.
step5.helpForm: Download blank VTR-41-A form from TxDMV
step5.helpExampleCaption: Example of a completed first reassignment block on the VTR-41-A form:

step6.title: WebDealer Submission
step6.why: WebDealer is the TxDMV online portal for submitting title and registration applications. All documents must be verified before submission.
step6.task1: Verify all checklist items are complete and accurate
step6.task2: Log into WebDealer and submit the title application
step6.check1: Bill of Sale signed by all parties
step6.check6: Odometer readings match across all documents
step6.check8: All fees accounted for (title, registration, doc fee)
step6.check9: Customer file details reviewed before WebDealer submission

step7.title: ePlates
step7.why: ePlates is the TxDMV system for assigning license plates. The plate number must be recorded for the customer's records.
step7.task1: Log back into WebDealer to find the assigned plate number
step7.task2: Assign a license plate to this vehicle
step7.task3: Record the plate number on all relevant paperwork
step7.task4: Print the temporary tag for the customer

step8.title: Issue Plates & Close Deal
step8.why: The final step: hand the plates to the customer and verify everything matches the file.
step8.task1: Hand license plates to the customer
step8.task2: Verify the plate number matches the records
step8.task3: Remind customer: inspection and insurance must stay current

start.fillRequired: Fill in every field marked with an asterisk.

start.notOnLot: Not on the lot? Enter a VIN
start.noBack: No back. The barcode never read.
start.scanRead: Read the {list} off the card. Check it against the ID.
start.scanNothingUsable: The barcode carried nothing we could use, so type the details.
start.scanNoCamera: No camera here, or it was refused. Type the details instead.
start.nothingRead: Nothing could be read off the barcode
start.saleStartedIdNot: The Sale Started. The ID Did Not.
start.openAndAdd: Open The Sale And Add It
start.frontIdAlt: The front of the ID now on file
start.backIdAlt: The back of the ID now on file
start.frontJustShot: The front of the ID just photographed
start.backJustShot: The back of the ID just photographed
start.asOnId: As it appears on their ID
start.titleChoose: Say what the title is before starting.
start.titleSalvageNote: A salvage vehicle that has not been rebuilt and inspected cannot be sold for the road.
start.titleUnverifiedBlock: This vehicle's title status has not been verified. Mark it on the inventory side, then start the sale.
start.titleUnsellableBlock: This vehicle cannot be sold with its current title.
start.titleKindCleanPaper: A Texas Certificate of Title with no brand in the remarks.
start.titleKindCleanNeeds: The ordinary packet. Nothing extra for the buyer.
start.titleKindRebuiltPaper: The remarks say REBUILT SALVAGE. It was salvage once and has been rebuilt and titled again.
start.titleKindRebuiltNeeds: The buyer also signs the Rebuilt Title Disclosure before anything else, and the notice goes on the window.
start.titleKindBondedPaper: The remarks say BONDED TITLE: a surety bond stood in for missing ownership papers.
start.titleKindBondedNeeds: The ordinary packet. The bond is ours, not the buyer's.
start.titleKindSalvagePaper: The paper is headed Salvage Vehicle Title, or the remarks say SALVAGE.
start.titleKindSalvageNeeds: The sale starts and holds. The title is rebuilt in our name first (the guide walks it), then the buyer signs like any rebuilt car.
start.titleKindNonrepairablePaper: The paper is headed Nonrepairable Vehicle Title, or the remarks say NONREPAIRABLE or JUNK.
start.titleKindNonrepairableNeeds: This car can never be titled for the road again, by anyone. It is sold for parts or scrap only, and not through this sale.
start.salvageWhat: What happens with the salvage title?
start.titleOriginLabel: The title is from another state
start.titleOriginChoose: Say which state issued the title.
start.titleOriginNeeds: Texas titles a car on another state's title only after a VIN inspection (Form VTR-68-A). The title step will say so.
start.titleTell1: Look at the top of the paper. A salvage car's title is headed Salvage Vehicle Title, not Certificate of Title.
start.titleTell2: Read the Remarks box on the front. REBUILT SALVAGE, BONDED TITLE, SALVAGE or nothing at all.
start.titleTell3: An out-of-state title says its brand on the front too; the words vary, the idea does not.
start.titleTell4: Still unsure? An NMVTIS or Carfax pull on the VIN says it in one line.
start.titleHoldNote: This sale will hold at the title until it is rebuilt in our name. Everything else can be done now.
start.confirmMailingBody: Read it back to the buyer before you start. A wrong address here means the title is mailed to somebody else.
start.idDidNotSaveConnection: The ID did not save. Check the connection.
start.vinLooksWrong: That VIN does not look right. It is 17 characters, no I, O or Q.
start.vinServiceUnreachable: Could not reach the VIN service. Fill the three fields in yourself.
start.checkAgainstCar: Check these against the car before you carry on.
start.pickCarOrVin: Pick the car, or enter a VIN.
start.needOdometer: Enter the odometer reading in miles.
start.vinLookingUp: Not on the lot. Looking up this VIN…
start.vinNoDecode: That VIN did not come back. Enter the car by hand.
start.vinPlaceholder: 17 characters, no I, O or Q

plan.registrationByQuestion: Who Files The Title And Registration?
plan.registrationByHelp: This decides most of the paperwork.
plan.registrationByBuyerGloss: They go to the county themselves
plan.titleSignedByHelp: The 130-U needs the buyer's signature. If they are not here to sign it, we sign for them under a power of attorney.
plan.titleSignedByBuyerGloss: They sign the 130-U on this screen or in ink
plan.titleSignedByDealerGloss: Adds a power of attorney to the packet
plan.priceIncludesRegistrationHelp: This is the figure they would owe us if the filing comes back to us later.
plan.insuranceShownQuestion: Did They Show Proof Of Insurance?
plan.salvagePathQuestion: What Happens With The Salvage Title?
plan.salvagePathHelp: This decides the whole packet. A salvage title cannot be assigned to a buyer for the road.
plan.salvagePathRebuildGloss: Rebuilt salvage title in our name, then a normal sale with the disclosure
plan.salvagePathTowAway: Sell it as salvage, tow-away only
plan.salvagePathTowAwayGloss: No plates, no registration, no 130-U. Needs a salvage dealer licence.
plan.salvagePathUndecidedGloss: Everything else can be done now. The documents wait.
plan.inspectionConfirmBody: Required Texas inspections must be satisfied before sale. The dealer remains responsible; this choice does not waive that duty. Safety inspections ended for non-commercial vehicles in 2025. Emissions and commercial requirements still apply where required. Confirm you understand and have checked this vehicle’s requirements or exemption.

meanings.rebuiltDisclosure: This says the car has a rebuilt title, in writing, before anything else is signed.
meanings.billOfSale: This is the bill of sale. It says what you are paying, what the car is, and that it is sold as is.
meanings.form130U: This is the state's title and registration application. It puts the car in your name.
meanings.vehicleResponsibility: This says you are filing the title and registration yourself, and what it costs if it comes back to us.
meanings.insuranceAcknowledgment: This says you did not show proof of insurance today, and that you will have it before you drive.
meanings.financing: This is the financing contract: the amount, the rate, the payments and when they are due.
meanings.salvageBillOfSale: This is the bill of sale for a salvage vehicle. It cannot be registered or driven until it is rebuilt and retitled.
meanings.towAwayAcknowledgment: This says the car leaves on a tow, and that no plates or registration come with it.
meanings.buyerResponsibilityStatement: This says the salvage title, the rebuild and any application to the state are yours from here.

ceremony.reuseConsent: Put the signature I drew on the earlier page on this document too. I have read this one to the end.
ceremony.downloadNote: Save your signed copies now. The dealer can also text you a private link for later.

badges.readyNormalGloss: The ordinary packet. Plates can be promised.
badges.readyRebuiltGloss: Rebuilt salvage title. The disclosure is in the packet on its own.
badges.rebuiltPacketIncompleteGloss: Salvage title being rebuilt in our name. No documents until the county's title arrives.
badges.doNotPromisePlatesGloss: Sold as salvage, tow-away only. No registration, no plates, no 130-U.
badges.decideSalvagePathGloss: Salvage title. Rebuild it first, or sell it as salvage to be towed away. The documents wait.
badges.cannotBeSoldGloss: This title cannot be titled for the road again by anyone.
badges.titleUnknownGloss: Nobody has looked at the title. No document files until somebody does.
